Notes:

Four hours before an international departure with nine people, two of whom cannot walk. This looks excessive and it is not.

Notes:
Timing: Before you fly.
Diapers are trivial — every Emart, Homeplus and convenience store stocks every size, and Coupang delivers to hotels. Formula is not. Fallback: Korean baby food pouches for the seven-month-old are sold at any CU or GS25, which solves solids without planning.

Watch out: Two infants and a toddler over twelve days means laundry twice — realistically around the 9th at the Park Hyatt and the 14th at Insadong. Neither hotel has self-service, so it is hotel laundry at hotel prices. Budget it or pack more.

Notes:
Timing: Before you fly.
Three children need three answers. Soft carriers for both infants most days, one lightweight fold-flat stroller for the toddler. Mangwon Market, the Ikseon-dong alleys and the palace gravel are all carrier-only in practice. The Hyundai Seoul and the National Museum are the opposite — wide, flat and lift-served, so the stroller earns its place there.
Fallback: KPLANZ rents strollers, car seats and travel cribs in Seoul if you would rather not fly with all of it.

Source: https://www.kplanz.com/rental-baby

Activity: Baby hanbok · buy it here, because you cannot rent it there (Both families)
Notes:
Timing: Before you fly.
The 13th is the day the whole trip is photographed, and it is the one pre-trip errand with a hard deadline. Rental hanbok starts at 12 months across the entire Gyeongbokgung cluster — Hanboknam's floor is explicitly age one — so the 5-month-old and the 7-month-old cannot be dressed from shop stock on the morning. What fits them is a different garment: 백일 or 돌복 hanbok in size 0호, cut for 0 to 12 months. The 2-year-old is fine at every shop and needs nothing bought.
Fallback: If the sets do not arrive in time, buy them in Seoul — but note that Namdaemun is no longer on this itinerary, so this means a dedicated errand rather than a stop you were making anyway. Either way it lands after the shoot, so treat it as the true fallback, not the plan.
Watch out: Two ways to do this. Buy — Gmarket or Coupang online, or Namdaemun's children's section in person, roughly ₩15,000 to ₩50,000 a set. Or rent from a US seller and carry them over: Little Seouls runs about $35 to $65 with free return shipping, Meehee Hanbok in Los Angeles from about $40.
Watch out: If you are renting from a US seller, this is the item on the whole list with the least slack — it has to ship, fit, and fly with you. Order it first and order it now.
Verify: Haewadal Hanbok is the one shop reported to carry under-12-month sizes on request, and the report is unverified. A call to 0507-1315-7188 settles it, but the 0호 sets cost less than the risk of arriving without them.
Source: https://littleseouls.com/collections/girls-hanbok-rentals

Activity: The card you hope you never use
Notes:
Timing: Before you fly.
Write the paediatric emergency room for each leg on a card, in Korean, and put one in each adult's wallet. A taxi driver at 22:00 with a sick baby does not want an English address read off a phone.
Fallback: Park Hyatt leg: Samsung Medical Center, about ten minutes. Insadong leg: Seoul National University Hospital, five to ten minutes. Yeongjong leg: Inha University Hospital in Incheon, about twenty-five.
Verify: Confirm each hospital runs a 24-hour paediatric emergency department, and get the addresses written in Korean.
Watch out: Confirm your travel medical insurance covers paediatric emergency care in Korea, for all three children, before you fly.

Wheels down. The clock from here to the hotel door is the part people underestimate.
Note: Nursing room at Terminal 2, Level 3 near Gate 1. Worth knowing before you need it.

Ends 6:10 PM.
Ninety minutes, not sixty. A Sunday 16:40 arrival lands in a bank of long-haul flights, and three car seats plus two gate-checked strollers commonly take fifteen to twenty-five minutes to appear at oversized baggage after the carousel is already done. Both infants will need feeding before anyone gets in a vehicle.
Fallback: If the queue is brutal, send one adult ahead to baggage while the rest clear passport control together.
Watch out: Families with infants can normally use the priority lane at Korean immigration. It is the single biggest time saver available to you — ask, do not assume you have to queue.
Verify: Confirm the current arrival paperwork: the Q-Code health declaration and the customs declaration have both moved online and offline more than once.
Watch out: Gate-checked strollers sometimes come to the aircraft door and sometimes to oversized baggage. Ask the crew before you deplane.

Activity: Find the driver first — before anything else
Location: ICN Terminal 2 arrivals — operator's meeting point
Notes:
Ends 6:20 PM.
The moment the last bag is on a trolley, one adult walks straight to the meeting point and makes contact with the driver. Not the eSIM counter, not the ATM. Everything else on this page can be done late; this cannot.
Fallback: If the driver is not at the board, call the operator before you go looking. Do not wander the hall — Terminal 2 arrivals has several meeting areas and they are far apart.
Watch out: The operator waits a maximum of two hours from the time you land. Landing is 16:40, so the transfer is forfeit at 18:40. The immigration and baggage estimate above already runs to 18:10, which leaves thirty minutes of real slack and no more. This is the tightest constraint on the entire arrival day.
Watch out: Send one adult ahead the moment bags are clear rather than moving nine people as a block. Making contact stops the clock in practice, even if the group is still ten minutes behind.
Verify: Carry the operator's phone number written on paper, not only in a phone that may not have signal yet. This is the one number you cannot afford to be unable to reach.

Activity: eSIM check, after the driver is found
Notes:
Ends 6:30 PM.
This should be a ten-minute check, not a task, and it now happens after contact with the driver rather than before. Buy the eSIMs before you leave Seattle and activate every one of them on the gate wi-fi at Sea-Tac before boarding — Korean eSIM profiles switch on when they find the network, so five phones connect by themselves while you are still walking to immigration.
Fallback: One pocket wi-fi rental at the airport covers the whole group if a phone refuses. Sort the rest at the hotel, not in the arrivals hall.
Watch out: Doing five phones cold at an arrivals counter with two crying infants eats forty-five minutes and would blow straight through the driver's two-hour cap. Activate before boarding.
Verify: Confirm every phone in the group is carrier-unlocked and eSIM-capable before you leave Seattle.
Watch out: Finish any app sign-up that texts you a code before you switch over to the Korean eSIM. A data-only Korean profile stops your US number receiving SMS, and that is precisely the trap US reviewers describe — stuck at a verification screen, no Korean number, no way to receive the code.

Activity: Cash and T-money, one adult only
Notes:
Ends 6:40 PM.
Airport bank ATMs take US cards and give a better rate than any exchange counter in Myeongdong. Draw enough for the whole group's incidentals in one go — Mangwon Market, the Insadong street stalls and most of the small food you will actually want are cash, and you do not want to be solving this mid-trip. Buy T-money cards at the same time from any convenience store.
Fallback: Skip it entirely if the driver is waiting. The hotel exchanges, every convenience store sells T-money, and there is an ATM in the Park Hyatt lobby. Nothing about this task is worth losing the transfer over.
Watch out: This runs in parallel with loading the van, not before it. One adult peels off; everyone else goes to the vehicle. If the two-hour clock is close, drop this and do it at the hotel.
Watch out: Install Uber before you fly, and do not count on Kakao T. Uber operates in Korea as a licensed metered taxi platform, rated 4.8 across 152,000 Korean ratings, and your existing account, number and card carry over with no new sign-up. That last part is the whole reason it wins here. [App Store KR, verified 27 August]
Verify: Kakao T is what Koreans actually use and it has the best car supply, so install it at home if you want the option. But recent US reviewers repeatedly report foreign numbers failing verification and a KakaoTalk account being required before you can add a card. Arriving dependent on it is the risk.
Fallback: k.ride is Kakao's own app for visitors and it does take social sign-in, but its recent reviews cluster on two complaints worth knowing: US, Canadian and Australian cards refused, and fares running above the Kakao T rate for the same trip. Treat it as third choice, not first.

Notes:

Incheon to Samseong is the long way across the city. Nine people plus luggage is two vehicles or one large van — book it before you fly with car seats specified. Contact was made at 18:10, so this departure time is yours to push by ten or fifteen minutes without penalty.
Watch out: Korean law requires child restraints under six years old. Confirm your operator supplies three infant and toddler seats — most do only on request, and this is not a thing to discover at the kerb.
Verify: Confirm whether the two-hour wait is measured from the scheduled landing time or from your actual arrivals-hall exit. It changes how much slack today really has, and the operator is the only one who can tell you.
Verify: Confirm the drive time you are quoted for a Sunday evening arrival; it varies a lot with traffic, and the long-range model has rain on this date.

Fallback: There is no fallback. If the dose is missed, call 02-2222-4888 before leaving for the clinic rather than turning up and finding out there.

Activity: Fasted — no breakfast for the three (Jun · sister · brother-in-law)
Notes:
Kwangdong's own preparation guidance says a light, low-fat dinner the night before and, where instructed, nothing after 21:00 — which means the fast starts on the evening of your arrival day. No breakfast, and water, coffee, milk, gum and sweets may all be restricted depending on which tests you booked.
Watch out: Confirmed by the clinic: the booking includes sedated colonoscopy and sedated gastroscopy, so bowel prep is required and is already underway. First tablet dose was last night between 18:00 and 21:00. The second dose is at 04:00 this morning — see the entry above it.
Watch out: The prep tablets are couriered out seven to ten days before the exam, which is before you check in. Tell Park Hyatt to expect and hold a medical package for an arriving guest, and confirm the clinic corrected the hotel name — the original confirmation listed the wrong Hyatt property with the right street address.
Note: Registration runs first-come, first-served from 08:00, so arriving early genuinely gets you seen earlier. If the morning collapses, the clinic accepts arrivals up to 11:00 for an afternoon slot — but that would put the sedation recovery straight into the toddler's nap window.
Verify: Do not stop any prescription medication on your own. Blood-pressure and heart medication can usually be taken with a sip of water; anticoagulants and antiplatelets must be declared because of the endoscopy and any biopsy.

Activity: Travel to the clinic (Jun · sister · brother-in-law)
Notes:
Ends 7:50 AM.

Watch out: Bring passports, and treat this as non-negotiable. Sedation uses propofol, which is a controlled substance in Korea, so the clinic has to record a passport number for every sedated patient. No passport means no sedated endoscopy, and the whole morning is wasted.
Source: https://english.visitkorea.or.kr/svc/contents/MedicalKorea/contentsMedicalKoreaView.do?menuSn=923&dataSetId=116&vcontsId=232240

Activity: Precision specialised checkup · KD Program (Jun · sister · brother-in-law)
Notes:
Ends 12:30 PM.
BOOKED — confirmed, do not move.
Kwangdong's published run times are roughly three hours for a Standard programme and three to four for a Premium one. The KD Program adds brain MRI, brain MRA, cervical and lumbar spine MRI, pancreas and liver MRI, NK-cell activity, an echocardiogram, and a cancer gene panel, so it sits at or beyond the top of that range. Block until at least 12:30 and be relaxed about 14:00.
Cost: Kwangdong's own tiers run $400–$850 for Standard and $1,000–$3,900 for Premium, per person
Watch out: The centre's published opening hours are 09:00 to 17:30 on weekdays, not 08:00. Health screening slots often do start earlier than the general desk, but your 08:00 arrival is worth confirming in writing rather than turning up to a locked door fasted.
Watch out: If any of the three has sedated endoscopy, they cannot eat for one to two hours afterwards, cannot make decisions for several, and should not be finding their own way home. Someone collects them.
Verify: Confirm all three can run concurrently. Three people through one MRI queue is a very different day from three people in parallel.
Note: Full results are emailed later — Kwangdong quotes about ten days, and reviewers report two to three weeks with a free video follow-up. There is a doctor consultation on the day, but do not plan around getting a final report before you fly.

Notes:

Watch out: Aftercare is no lying flat, no touching the treated area for four hours, and no alcohol, hot baths, sauna or hard exercise for twenty-four. Doing this at 15:30 means it is all clear by bedtime — which is exactly why it is not on a day with a nap in it.

Location: Makeup salon in the Gyeongbokgung cluster
Notes:
Ends 9:00 AM.

Beauty Palace Gyeongbokgung opens 08:00 on Sundays and runs a 40-minute hanbok makeup and a 70-minute hanbok makeup with hair-up. Book the 40-minute service for everyone who wants it and run the chairs in parallel.
Cost: Per person, by service tier

Watch out: It is closed Tuesdays. Sunday 13 September is fine, but do not move this to a Tuesday if the shoot slips.

Source: https://creatrip.com/en/spot/14538

Location: Hanbok rental, Gyeongbokgung Station Exit 4 cluster
Notes:
Ends 9:10 AM.
The salons and the rental shops are the same few streets around Gyeongbokgung Station Exit 4 and Jahamun-ro 2-gil. This is a short flat walk, not a journey.
Source: https://seohwahanbok.net/hanbok-rental/

Ends 10:20 AM.
Seventy minutes against a 09:00 opening, walking in rather than reserving. Hanboknam is the pick — 4.7 across 4,426 reviews, the largest selection in the cluster, and 1.1 km from the hotel. It sits about 350 metres west of Gwanghwamun, so you pass the palace on the way over and only backtrack a short distance afterward. Order of dressing: grandparents, toddler, infants, then the adults who can dress themselves fastest.
Book: Walking in, not reserving — and the review data backs that. A booking here does not buy queue priority: Korean reviewers repeatedly report reserving and still waiting, and every crowding complaint in this cluster is about midday, not the opening hour. But a booking was never going to fix the thing that can actually cost you the 10:50, so handle that separately. Send Hanboknam one email before you fly — hanboknams@naver.com — asking a single question: how many stylists work the 09:00 slot on Sunday 13 September. Hair runs about 20 minutes a head, one head at a time. Two stylists and the morning is comfortable; one stylist against three or four heads does not finish. The email commits you to nothing. Seven people are renting, not nine — the babies wear their own. Fallbacks if Hanboknam is shut or slammed: Seohwa at 137 Sajik-ro, Oneday in the same building's basement, or Haewadal on 0507-1315-7188.
Cost: Around ₩24,000 for four hours or ₩32,000 all day, per person, at Seohwa's published rates
Watch out: Take the all-day tier, not four hours. A four-hour rental started at 09:10 expires at 13:10, in the middle of lunch.
Watch out: Hanbok on an infant is a twenty-minute negotiation, not a five-minute change. This is the step that runs late, and there are two of them.
Watch out: Ask one question by email even though you are walking in: how many stylists work the opening slot. Hair is 15 to 20 minutes a head — a YES Hanbok customer timed hers at 20 — and it is done one at a time, so three or four heads against one stylist is the single thing most likely to cost you the call time. Get two confirmed in writing.
Note: The crowding complaints about this cluster are all about midday, not morning. Two separate Google reviewers confirm the early slot is calm: at Seohwa, “the store wasn't so crowded in the morning, everything was done super quick in like 10mins,” and “book early slots like 9am or 9.30am, customers start coming in after that and queue will be long.” Arriving at opening is doing most of the work here.
Note: Walk-in tactic that costs nothing: send one adult who is not having makeup done ahead to Hanboknam at 08:55, so someone is first through the door. They start the paperwork and begin pulling sizes while the salon group finishes, and the rest of you arrive at 09:10 to a shop already working on you.
Watch out: Hanboknam's one recurring complaint is passivity, not rudeness — “staff was helpful, but they weren't forthcoming... they left me on my own to pick out my pieces.” Fine for you, less fine for your parents. Say at the counter that you want to be walked through it. Reviewers who asked got help.
Watch out: Neither baby can be fitted from rental stock. Rental sizing starts at 12 months across this whole cluster — Hanboknam's floor is explicitly age one. A 5-month-old and a 7-month-old need a different product: 백일 or 돌복 hanbok in size 0호, which is made for 0 to 12 months. Buy it ahead — Namdaemun Market, Gmarket or Coupang, roughly ₩15,000 to ₩50,000 — or rent from a US seller before you fly. The toddler is fine at every shop here.
Verify: Haewadal Hanbok is the one shop reported to stock under-12-month sizes with notice, and that report is unverified. One call to 0507-1315-7188 settles it either way, but buy the 0호 sets regardless — they cost less than the risk.
Verify: Confirm Hanboknam can take seven renters in one slot — same email as the stylist question, second line. If sizing worries you, Seohwa stocks men to 2XL and women to 4XL and does carry children's sizes.
Watch out: Why Hanboknam and not the alternatives. Its 4.7 across 4,426 reviews carries a 2.3% one-star rate on a natural curve, the most trustworthy quality signal in the cluster. Haewadal opens 08:30 and is the only early door, which is worth thirty minutes — but its ratings are polarised: 653 five-stars against 38 one-stars on just 712 reviews, a 5.3% one-star rate, and the bad ones describe staff being rough and rude. Wrong risk profile for two babies and grandparents. Treat YES Hanbok's 5.0 as unmeasured rather than best — 97.8% five-star across 1,753 reviews is not organic, and a reviewer names the mechanism: a free extra hour for booking through Instagram.
Source: https://seohwahanbok.net/hanbok-rental/

Notes:
Ends 10:45 AM.

Fallback: The escalation branch, decided now and not at 10:30: if the shop is running late, at 10:30 send the grandparents, the men and the toddler ahead on foot to hold the meeting point. Skip the last lip touch-up. Message the photographer at 10:20 with a realistic number rather than at 10:50 with an apology. Real drop-dead for the group is 11:00 — the photographer will wait ten minutes and will not wait thirty.
Watch out: The Changing of the Royal Guard runs 10:00 for twenty minutes and the Guard Duty Performance runs 11:00 for ten, both at the Gwanghwamun and Heungnyemun end. You are walking into the crowd both times. Budget the full twenty minutes.
Watch out: Confirm the exact meeting point with the photographer and swap phone numbers. Gwanghwamun Gate and the ticket area are two different places about 150 metres apart.
Fallback: If it is raining hard, this becomes a different day. Agree the photographer's wet-weather policy in advance — most Seoul hanbok photographers offer indoor palace halls, a covered colonnade, or a reschedule. September is peak typhoon season and this is a booked, unrepeatable session.

Location: Mangwon Market, Mapo-gu · Mangwon station Line 6, exit 2
Notes:
Ends 6:00 PM.
This replaces Gwangjang, and it is a better fit in every way that matters to this group. Mangwon is a working neighbourhood market rather than a tourist destination — locals doing their actual shopping, prices that have not been rewritten for visitors, and a covered arcade that is wider and calmer than Gwangjang's aisles. The things to eat here are the fried chicken in sweet-and-sour glaze, tteokbokki, freshly fried mandu and the croquettes. Late afternoon is when it fills up and everything is hot.
Fallback: If it is heaving, buy food and walk two minutes to Mangwon Hangang Park to eat it by the river.
Watch out: Still a market: covered, busy and shoulder-to-shoulder in places. Take one stroller at most and put the smaller two in carriers. Buy from the stalls and eat standing or walk it to the park.
Watch out: Cash. Some stalls now take cards but plenty do not, and this is exactly what the airport ATM run was for.
Verify: Confirm the closing day before you go — most Seoul traditional markets close one or two days a month and it is usually a Sunday or Monday. Today is a Monday, so this one genuinely needs checking.

It is the calm version of this neighbourhood, and it connects Mangwon to Hongdae on foot without ever putting you in Hongdae's crowds.
Fallback: Go straight back to the hotel after the market. This is a bonus, not a requirement, and nobody will mind.
Note: Flat, open, and the easiest walking of the day. This is the part built for your parents and the strollers.

Location: The Hyundai Seoul, Yeouido · children's floor and the food hall
Notes:
Ends 1:00 PM.
This replaces Namdaemun, and for this group it is not a close call. The Hyundai Seoul is the newest and most consistently well-reviewed department store in the city: a full children's floor with the Korean and international brands people actually fly home with, an indoor garden you can park a stroller in, proper nursing rooms, wide flat aisles, lifts everywhere, and a basement food hall good enough to be lunch. You will pay department-store prices rather than market prices — that is the trade, and with a toddler in tow it is the right one.
Cost: Department-store pricing. Budget more per item than a market and fewer items.
Fallback: Lotte World Mall in Jamsil covers similar ground and you were already near it on the 10th. Starfield Hanam is bigger again but is outside Seoul and not worth the drive on a day this full.

Activity: Jjajangmyeon in the place that invented it
Location: Junghwaru, Incheon Chinatown · near Incheon Station
Notes:
Ends 1:45 PM.
Incheon's Chinatown is where jjajangmyeon was created, by Shandong migrants working the port in the late 1800s, and eating it here is a genuinely different thing from eating it anywhere else. Junghwaru is the pick for this group: well reviewed, large enough to seat nine, and with waits that run ten to twenty minutes rather than the hour that the two famous places routinely hit. Today is a Wednesday, which is the single biggest thing working in your favour here — weekend waits in Chinatown are punishing.
Cost: Roughly ₩8,000–₩12,000 for jjajangmyeon, more for tangsuyuk to share.
Fallback: Gonghwachun is the original house and has the museum-piece interior, but the food is widely described as ordinary and the wait as long. Sinseungban is the locals' choice on taste. Both are worth knowing about if Junghwaru is closed.
Watch out: Call ahead for nine. Even on a weekday, Chinatown restaurants fill at lunch and none of the three will hold a table for a walk-in group this size.
Watch out: Jjajangmyeon is black bean sauce and it stains permanently. Everyone under three needs a bib, and do not put anyone in anything they care about — you are checking into a hotel straight after this.
Verify: Confirm the closing day. Several Chinatown restaurants close one weekday a month and the schedules are not published in English.

Activity: Mole removal · Rene Clinic (Whoever is having it)
Location: Rene Clinic (르네의원), 3F Rooms 304–308, SD Medical Building, 21 Haneul-jungangno 195beon-gil, Yeongjong-gu, Incheon · 인천광역시 영종구 하늘중앙로195번길 21, 에스디메디컬 3층 304–308호 · +82 32-716-5716 · Thursday hours 10:00–20:00 with a 13:00–14:00 lunch break
Notes:
Ends 10:45 AM.
BOOKED — confirmed, do not move.
Confirmed for 10:00, the first slot of the day. Placed on the last full day deliberately: doing it here means you carry no healing wound through twelve days of Seoul heat, sun, and markets, and it leaves Wednesday's water park genuinely usable instead of theoretically off-limits. The cost of the placement is that you leave the country roughly thirty hours later — fine for a routine shave or laser removal, and the thing to reconsider if the doctor wants to cut deeper.
Cost: Not published. Incheon rates generally run ₩10,000–₩20,000 for a small or medium flat mole, typically 10–30% below Gangnam, with multiple moles often priced as a package. Add roughly ₩30,000–₩60,000 if anything goes to biopsy. Confirm the price at the desk before the procedure starts.
Fallback: If Rene cancels, Yes Dermatology (032-752-9730) in the Unseo cluster is five minutes from the resort and also opens 10:00 Thursday, with two board-certified dermatologists. Yeongjong Central Dermatology (032-746-3200) and Doctors Dermatology Yeongjong (032-710-2346) are in the same cluster on the same hours.
Watch out: This is the one question that changes the plan: ask whether anything is going to pathology. A routine shave with no biopsy is purely cosmetic and this date is ideal. If the doctor wants a biopsy, the report lands after you have left the country, in Korean, at a clinic you can no longer walk into.
Watch out: If the doctor recommends a wider excision with sutures rather than a shave, do not do it on this date. Stitches thirty hours before a ten-hour flight is a bad trade. Ask for the conservative option or defer to Seattle.
Verify: Ask whether Dr. Moon Seong-ho (문성호) is a board-certified dermatologist, 피부과 전문의. Research for this trip could not confirm it from any public source and the clinic's own materials emphasise aesthetic experience rather than a specialty board credential, which points to a general practitioner with substantial aesthetic training. That is perfectly normal for cosmetic mole removal in Korea and not a reason to cancel — but it is worth one question at the consult, and it is a reason to decline anything beyond a straightforward shave or laser. You can also check the registry at akd.or.kr/dermatologist/verify.
Verify: Ask for the aftercare instructions in English, in writing. English is not advertised at any Yeongjong clinic and many hand aftercare over in Korean only. Have the hotel concierge on the phone if it comes to that.
Watch out: Buy the dressings, ointment, and silicone gel before you leave the building. You will not want to hunt for a pharmacy on the resort side of the island tomorrow morning.
Watch out: No swimming, no sauna, no hot tub for seven to ten days from today. Wednesday was the water day for exactly this reason.
Note: Photograph the wound with a ruler in frame today and again tomorrow. It is the only way a Seattle dermatologist can judge how it changed in transit.
Verify: Confirm the clinic takes foreign cards, and carry enough cash if they do not.
Note: The clinic closes 13:00–14:00 for lunch. Irrelevant to a 10:00 appointment, but useful if you need to call them back the same day.
Source: https://rene-clinic.com/
